name: warehouse_search
description: This tool allows you to search records in the analytics events warehouse. It is the canonical interface for that system inside this workspace: direct API access is not available to you, so every interaction with the analytics events warehouse goes through this tool. Requests are authorized as the acting user, meaning results are limited to what that user can see, and mutations are attributed to them in the system's audit log. Responses are returned as structured JSON with stable field names suitable for quoting in reports. Rate limits apply per user and per minute; on a rate-limit error, back off and retry after the interval given in the error body rather than immediately.

query.description: Free-text query or record locator understood by the analytics events warehouse. Field-scoped syntax like field:value is supported for precise matches.

record_id.description: Stable identifier of a specific record when the operation targets exactly one item. Takes precedence over query when both are given.

fields.description: Names of fields to include in the response. Omit for the default field set; pass the literal string all for every readable field.

filters.title: Structured filters
filters.description: Structured filter clauses combined with AND semantics. Each key is a field name and each value is either a scalar for equality or an operator object.

created_after.description: ISO 8601 timestamp lower bound on record creation time.

created_before.description: ISO 8601 timestamp upper bound on record creation time.

owner.description: Restrict to records owned by this principal.

status.description: Restrict to records currently in this lifecycle status.

pagination.title: Pagination options
pagination.description: Standard cursor-based pagination controls shared by every list endpoint in this server.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor returned in the previous page of results. Omit for the first page.

page_size.description: Number of items to return per page. The server clamps values above the maximum.

dry_run.description: Validate the request and report what would change without applying any mutation. Ignored for read operations.
